Checklist.disclaimer: This list is just a suggestion and doesn't claim to be complete. Add your own tasks below for whatever matters in your situation.

passport.label: Passport / ID valid (at least 6 months)
passport.hint: Many countries require at least 6 months of remaining validity

visa.label: Visa applied for (if needed)
visa.hint: Foreign Office: entry and visa requirements by destination

insurance.label: International health insurance arranged
insurance.hint: Consumer advice center: comparison & guidance on international health insurance

ehic.label: European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) applied for
ehic.hint: For EU countries, free from your health insurer

deregister.label: Deregister residence (if moving away permanently)
deregister.hint: Saves the broadcasting fee and may bring tax benefits

taxid.label: Tax ID noted (stays valid for life)

bank_foreign.label: Account with free international Visa opened

bank_notify.label: Bank informed about your stay abroad
bank_notify.hint: Prevents your card from being blocked

cash.label: Some cash in local currency obtained

emergency_fund.label: Emergency fund (3 months of expenses) in a separate account
emergency_fund.hint: Why and how much to save

wise.label: Wise / Revolut card for cheap international transfers

pin.label: PIN of all cards memorized (no photo of it!)

backupcard.label: A second card packed as backup

bafoeg.label: Study-abroad grant application filed (if applicable)
bafoeg.hint: Official grant portal with funding calculator

creditrecognition.label: Credit recognition clarified with home university

socialsecurity.label: Social security in destination country researched

taxabroad.label: Double taxation agreement checked
taxabroad.hint: Federal Ministry of Finance: international tax law

housing.label: Accommodation secured for the first weeks

deposit.label: Deposit rules in destination country checked

rentalcontract.label: Rental contract fully read and understood

registration.label: Registered with the local residents' office (check local requirement)

copies.label: All important documents backed up digitally (cloud)

embassy.label: German embassy in destination country noted

vpn.label: VPN installed (for safe banking on foreign WiFi)

elster.label: Tax portal access set up (for tax returns)

roaming.label: EU roaming activated or local SIM planned

Spartipps.introDesc: {count} short statements about your habits — swipe right if they apply to you, left if not. At the end you'll get your personal savings plan.
Spartipps.habitsFound: {count, plural, one {# habit} other {# habits}} with savings potential found.
Spartipps.doingWell: You're already doing a lot right!
Spartipps.fallbackIdeas: Here are 3 ideas anyway that pay off for most people.

bank.statement: You still pay monthly account fees.
bank.tip: Switch to a free online account (e.g. a fee-free digital bank) — saves real money with no loss of convenience.

subs.statement: You have streaming or app subscriptions you barely use.
subs.tip: Check your subscription tracker and cancel anything you haven't used in 4 weeks.

phone.statement: Your phone plan costs more than €15 a month.
phone.tip: Discount providers often use the same network for half the price.

groceries.statement: You mostly buy brand-name products instead of store brands.
groceries.tip: Store brands are often identical and 20–30% cheaper.

impulse.statement: You often order online on impulse, without comparing prices.
impulse.tip: 24h rule: put it in the cart, buy it the next day only if you still want it.

car.statement: You mostly drive short distances (under 3 km) by car.
car.tip: Cycling or public transit saves not just fuel but parking fees too.

lunch.statement: You eat out for lunch almost every day.
lunch.tip: Meal prepping on the weekend quickly saves €100+ a month.

coffee.statement: You get a coffee-to-go every day.
coffee.tip: Your own thermos pays for itself in under 2 weeks.

compare.statement: You rarely compare prices before bigger purchases.
compare.tip: Price comparison sites often reveal alternatives 10–20% cheaper.

gym.statement: You use your gym less than once a week.
gym.tip: Many gyms offer flexible 10-visit passes instead of a fixed membership.

cashback.statement: You rarely use discount codes or cashback when shopping online.
cashback.tip: Browser extensions automatically find voucher codes at checkout.

roaming.statement: You paid for roaming on your last trip abroad.
roaming.tip: EU roaming is free — outside the EU, a local eSIM helps.

used.statement: You mostly buy electronics & furniture new instead of used.
used.tip: Refurbished devices are up to 40% cheaper and nearly like new.

books.statement: You buy books instead of borrowing them.
books.tip: Public libraries (including digital lending) are usually free.

standby.statement: Devices at your place often sit in standby instead of being fully off.
standby.tip: Switchable power strips can save up to 10% on electricity costs.

earlybird.statement: You usually book flights or trains at short notice.
earlybird.tip: Booking early saves 20–30% on average — plan big trips ahead.

split.statement: You settle shared or roommate costs manually and unclearly.
split.tip: Use Splittr to split expenses fairly and transparently with your group.

insurance.statement: You rarely or never compare insurance plans.
insurance.tip: An annual insurance comparison often reveals €100+ in savings potential.
